action_items: Fix SignalChart TradingView render regression (see rca_of_the_issue): in the effect, do not call setFailed(true) on the cancelled path - change `if (cancelled || !window.TradingView) { setFailed(true); return; }` to `if (cancelled) return; if (!window.TradingView) { setFailed(true); return; }`. React 18 StrictMode double-invokes the effect; the first (cleaned-up) instance's promise resolution flips failed=true and unmounts the container of the widget created by the second instance.
Reword the chart fallback copy to remove the 'renders fine on the deployed site' developer note.
Optional: add a visible 'click to enlarge' affordance / lightbox for the 3 small proof screenshots.

rca_of_the_issue: SignalChart uses a module-level promise for tv.js and a per-effect `cancelled` flag. Under React 18 StrictMode (enabled in src/index.js), the effect mounts, cleans up (cancelled=true), then mounts again. When the shared promise resolves, the first, cancelled instance executes `if (cancelled || !window.TradingView) { setFailed(true); return; }` -> failed=true. React then unmounts the widget container div (rendered only when !failed), so the TradingView iframe created by the second instance is hidden and the fallback text is shown, despite tv.js (200) and widgetembed (200) loading fine. Fix: separate the cancelled guard from the failure guard.
